For example: an `ApplyGuardrail` call with 1000 characters of text and 3 guardrails would generate 3 text units of consumption per guardrail per safeguard in the guardrail.\\n\\n Member account calls using the Amazon Bedrock Policy will count towards the Service Quotas for the member account. Review the Service Quotas Console or Service Quotas documentation and be sure that your Guardrails runtime limits are sufficient for your call volume.\\n\\n**What happens if I have both organization-level and account-level enforced guardrails as well as a guardrail in my request?**\\n: All 3 guardrails will be enforced at runtime. The net effect is a union of all guardrails, with the most restrictive control taking precedence.\\n\\n This applies to guardrails enforced at *different levels* \u2014 organization, account, and request. It does not describe multiple Amazon Bedrock policies attached at different points in your organization hierarchy. Those are resolved by AWS Organizations into a single effective policy before enforcement, rather than combined. See the note in Organization-level enforcement.\\n\\n**When should I use selective or comprehensive guarding control?**\\n: Use **Selective** when you trust callers to tag the right content and want to reduce unnecessary guardrail processing. This is useful when callers handle a mix of pre-validated and user-generated content, and only need guardrails applied to specific portions. Use **Comprehensive** when you want to enforce guardrails on everything, regardless of what the caller tags. This is the safer default when you don't want to rely on callers to correctly identify sensitive content.\\n\\n**How can I include or exclude certain models from enforcement?**\\n: Use the model enforcement control to scope which models on Amazon Bedrock a guardrail applies to for inference. If not configured, enforcement applies to all models on Amazon Bedrock by default. This control accepts the following lists:\\n\\n * **Included models:** Models to enforce the guardrail on. Accepts specific model identifiers or the keyword `ALL` to explicitly include all models. When empty, enforcement applies to all models.\\n * **Excluded models:** Models to exclude from guardrail enforcement. A version is a snapshot of your guardrail that you create at a point in time\\nwhen you are iterating on the working draft of the guardrail. Create versions of your guardrail when you are satisfied\\nwith a set of configurations.\\n\\nYou can use the test window (for more information,\\nsee Test your guardrail) to compare how different versions of your\\nguardrail perform when evaluating the input prompts and model responses, and generating controlled responses for\\nthe final output. When you use versions, you can switch between different configurations for your guardrail, and update\\nyour application with the most appropriate version for your use case.\\n\\nThe following topics discuss how to create a version of your guardrail when it's ready for deployment, view\\ninformation about it, and delete it when you no longer want to use it.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nGuardrail versions aren't separate resources and don't have their own ARN. A guardrail ARN\\ndoesn't include a version, so the `Resource` element of an IAM policy can't target\\nan individual version. It applies to the guardrail and all of its versions.\\n\\nTo restrict access to a specific guardrail version, use the\\n`bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier` condition key, which accepts the guardrail ARN with an\\noptional `:version` suffix. For more information, see\\nEnforce the use of specific guardrails in model\\ninference requests.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* Create a version of a guardrail\\n* View information about guardrail versions\\n* Delete a version of a guardrail\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-deploy.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Check Bedrock guardrail version quota docs"}

These\\nquotas are fixed. They aren't managed in Service Quotas, and you can't request an\\nincrease.\\n\\nGuardrail quotas\\n\\n| Resource | Quota |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Guardrail policies per account | 200 |\\n| Policy name | 1 to 100 characters |\\n| Policy description | Up to 200 characters |\\n| Denied topics per policy | 30 |\\n| Denied topic name | 1 to 100 characters |\\n| Denied topic definition | Up to 240 characters |\\n| Example phrases per denied topic | 5, up to 160 characters each |\\n| Word filter entries per policy | 1,000 |\\n| Word filter entry | 1 to 50 characters, with no leading or trailing spaces |\\n| Assignments per import file | 500 |\\n| Assignments per download file | 10,000 |\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/guardrails.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Apply cross-account safeguards with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails enforcements\",\"context\":\"## Frequently Asked Questions\\n\\n**How is consumption towards quotas calculated when enforced guardrails apply?**\\n: Consumption will be calculated per guardrail ARN associated with each request and will be counted towards the AWS account making the API call. For example: an `ApplyGuardrail` call with 1000 characters of text and 3 guardrails would generate 3 text units of consumption per guardrail per safeguard in the guardrail.\\n\\n Member account calls using the Amazon Bedrock Policy will count towards the Service Quotas for the member account. Review the Service Quotas Console or Service Quotas documentation and be sure that your Guardrails runtime limits are sufficient for your call volume.\\n\\n**What happens if I have both organization-level and account-level enforced guardrails as well as a guardrail in my request?**\\n: All 3 guardrails will be enforced at runtime. The net effect is a union of all guardrails, with the most restrictive control taking precedence.\\n\\n This applies to guardrails enforced at *different levels* \u2014 organization, account, and request. It does not describe multiple Amazon Bedrock policies attached at different points in your organization hierarchy. Those are resolved by AWS Organizations into a single effective policy before enforcement, rather than combined. See the note in Organization-level enforcement.\\n\\n**When should I use selective or comprehensive guarding control?**\\n: Use **Selective** when you trust callers to tag the right content and want to reduce unnecessary guardrail processing. This is useful when callers handle a mix of pre-validated and user-generated content, and only need guardrails applied to specific portions. Use **Comprehensive** when you want to enforce guardrails on everything, regardless of what the caller tags. This is the safer default when you don't want to rely on callers to correctly identify sensitive content.\\n\\n**How can I include or exclude certain models from enforcement?**\\n: Use the model enforcement control to scope which models on Amazon Bedrock a guardrail applies to for inference. If not configured, enforcement applies to all models on Amazon Bedrock by default. This control accepts the following lists:\\n\\n * **Included models:** Models to enforce the guardrail on. Accepts specific model identifiers or the keyword `ALL` to explicitly include all models. When empty, enforcement applies to all models.\\n * **Excluded models:** Models to exclude from guardrail enforcement. When empty, no models are excluded.\\n\\n If a model appears in both lists, it is excluded.\\n\\n**When\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-enforcements.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Deploy your guardrail\",\"context\":\"# Deploy your guardrail\\n\\nWhen you're ready to deploy your guardrail to production, you create a version of it and invoke the version\\nof the guardrail in your application. A version is a snapshot of your guardrail that you create at a point in time\\nwhen you are iterating on the working draft of the guardrail. Create versions of your guardrail when you are satisfied\\nwith a set of configurations.\\n\\nYou can use the test window (for more information,\\nsee Test your guardrail) to compare how different versions of your\\nguardrail perform when evaluating the input prompts and model responses, and generating controlled responses for\\nthe final output. When you use versions, you can switch between different configurations for your guardrail, and update\\nyour application with the most appropriate version for your use case.\\n\\nThe following topics discuss how to create a version of your guardrail when it's ready for deployment, view\\ninformation about it, and delete it when you no longer want to use it.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nGuardrail versions aren't separate resources and don't have their own ARN. A guardrail ARN\\ndoesn't include a version, so the `Resource` element of an IAM policy can't target\\nan individual version. It applies to the guardrail and all of its versions.\\n\\nTo restrict access to a specific guardrail version, use the\\n`bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier` condition key, which accepts the guardrail ARN with an\\noptional `:version` suffix. For more information, see\\nEnforce the use of specific guardrails in model\\ninference requests.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* Create a version of a guardrail\\n* View information about guardrail versions\\n* Delete a version of a guardrail\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-deploy.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"ListGuardrails\",\"context\":\"# ListGuardrails\\n\\nLists details about all the guardrails in an account. {"id": "d46efa53-c1a3-4bf8-87e4-e768aa27b289", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I couldn't confirm that this limit can be raised, and the evidence I found points to it being fixed.

- **Service Quotas:** I listed the Bedrock quotas for this account in us-east-1. The only guardrail quota there is a runtime one, the ApplyGuardrail contextual grounding text-unit burst rate. There is no "versions per guardrail" quota, so there's nothing to request an increase on. An adjustable quota would normally appear there.
- **Documentation:** I couldn't find a documented figure for versions per guardrail. The general Bedrock quotas page is too large for me to read in full. From memory, the cap is about 20 versions per guardrail and isn't adjustable, but that is recollection and not something I verified. Your error at 19 published versions could mean the count includes something else, such as the working draft. I haven't checked that either.

**Likely fix:** delete old versions you no longer need, then rerun the job.
1. List the versions with `ListGuardrails`, passing the guardrail ARN as `guardrailIdentifier`.
2. Confirm which versions your applications still reference. Check app configs, Lambda environment variables and agent configs.
3. Remove the stale ones with `DeleteGuardrail`, passing a `guardrailVersion`. That deletes only that version and leaves the guardrail intact.
4. Add a prune step to the nightly job, for example keep the last N versions and delete the rest. Otherwise it will hit the cap again.

Also consider whether you need a new version every night. If the draft hasn't changed since the last version, you could skip creating one. Another option is to create versions only on real configuration changes.

If you want a definitive answer on raising the limit, you can open an AWS Support case. I can help with that if you'd like.

I can't delete resources from here, so the cleanup has to be done by you or the job itself. I can help you work out which versions are safe to remove.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
